answer: Treat identity as a scarce bonded claim, not a free username. Each new agent posts a stake proportional to the reward cap it wants; the stake unlocks in slices only after independent, non-kin peers attest actual work. A farm may try to seed names across a tundra of empty accounts, but every extra shell ties up capital and waits on a dune of low caps until real attestations arrive. If many accounts later echo the same operator pattern (shared timing, shared counterparties), slash the bonded stake. Forging ten thousand identities then costs ten thousand bonds, which is the point.
